s: Solothurn (the capital city of Solothurn canton, Switzerland)

solvent.et: Ultimately from Latin solvens. In German possibly a backformation from insolvent.

s: sol, the fifth step in the solfège scale of C, preceded by fa and followed by la.
Sol.et: Borrowed from Latin sol(ve) in the hymn for St. John the Baptist where all note names were taken from.

s: sol, a type of colloid in which a solid is dispersed in a liquid.
any pay or salary of a soldier
Schon am Zahltag hatte der junge Husarenkorporal seinen ganzen Wochensold versoffen.
Already on payday the young hussar corporal had spent his entire weekly pay on drink.
the daily basic pay of a soldier who serves less than two years, including (until 2011) conscripts as well as those rendering the substitute service (Zivildienst)
Er ist ein schamloser Lobbyist im Sold der Wirtschafts- und Finanzelite.
He is a shameless lobbiyst on the payroll of the economic and financial elite.
Sold.et: From Middle High German solt, from Old French solt, from Latin solidus (“a Roman gold coin”).

Sole.et: From Middle High German sol, sul, borrowed from Middle Low German sōle, sāle (“saltwater, brine”). Cognate with German Low German Söle, Sööl (“brine, pickling”).

to be recommended (to do something); to be asked (to do something)
to be intended (to do something); to be meant (to be something)

Es soll da viele Leute geben.

would; indicates that the subordinate clause indicates something that would happen in the past but after the time frame of the main clause
should; indicates that the subordinate clause indicates a hypothetical and unlikely condition for the main clause

s: snowbell, any plant of the genus Soldanella
Soldanelle.et: Borrowed from Italian soldanella, from the coin soldo because of the leaf form.

s: Mach das ruhig erst fertig, ich lese solang(e) Zeitung.
Just go ahead and finish that; I'll read the paper in the meantime.
Ich werde dich unterstützen, solange ich lebe.
I'll support you as long as I live.
as long as: provided that, assuming
Solange du mich nicht störst, ist mir egal was du machst.
Provided that you don't disturb me I don't care what you do.
pickled egg, cooked egg conserved in salted water
sunbed, tanning bed (device emitting ultraviolet radiation)
solarium, tanning salon (establishment where one can rent sunbeds)
Solarium.et: Ultimately from Latin solarium. Doublet of Söller.

s: Zwischen Stadt und Käufer des ehemaligen Theaters gab es Sollbruchstellen, vor allem war aber das Interesse an einer Eskalation nach den damals noch frischen Erfahrungen der Hafenstraße eher überschaubar.
Trump selbst warnte in einem Interview, seine Anhänger könnten eine gegen ihn womöglich verhängte Gefängnisstrafe als „Sollbruchstelle“ auffassen.
Trump himself warned in an interview that his supporters could see a possible prison sentence against him as a “breaking point”.
using thermal energy from the Sun

solitär.et: From French solitaire (“solitary”), from Latin sōlitārius.

s: a municipality of Lower Austria, Austria
raised deck or terrace, large balcony supported by walls or columns
Nach der Mahlzeit zog Julie sich zurück, es war längst Nacht, mit ihrer Kerze im irdenen Leuchter verließ sie den Söller, kühl wie eine Klosterfrau.
Söller.et: From Middle High German sölre, solre, from Old High German solāri, from Latin solarium. Cognate with Dutch zolder. Doublet of Solarium.

Sollwert.et: sollen (“to be supposed to, to be intended to; should”) + Wert (“value”)

s: solitaire ring (a ring with a single brilliant-cut diamond in a prong setting)
soldier's braid (military hairstyle common in the 18th and early 19th centuries)
martial, soldierlike (relating to or characteristic of soldiers)
a band of marauding, unscrupulous soldiers
the mentality of such soldiers, the marauding and war crimes themselves
Soldateska.et: 17th century, from Italian soldatesca. Doublet of soldatisch, which has quite the opposite sense of “soldierly”.

s: solifidianism (the soteriological doctrine that Christians are justified by faith alone)
A female person from Solingen or of Solingen descent
a native or inhabitant of Solingen
a native or inhabitant of Solothurn
The Solz (either of two tributaries in Hesse, Germany; both of which are tributaries of the river Fulda)
Solz.et: First attested in Latin as in terminis fluvii Sulza (“at the end of the rivulet Solz”) in the year 960 AD, from Old High German sulza (“saltwater, brine”). Doublet with Sole.

s: fixed borrowing rate period, fixed debit interest rate period (the duration for which the borrowing rate of a loan is contractually fixed)
Nach Ablauf der Sollzinsbindung kann der Kreditnehmer den Darlehensvertrag oft mit einer Frist von einem Monat kündigen.
After the fixed borrowing rate period expires, the borrower can often terminate the loan contract with one month's notice.
Sollzinsbindung.et: From Sollzins (“borrowing rate, debit interest”) + Bindung (“binding, fixing”).

s: borrowing rate, debit interest (interest charged by a lender to a borrower for a loan or overdrawn account)
Wenn das Girokonto überzogen wird, berechnet die Bank einen hohen Sollzins.
If the checking account is overdrawn, the bank charges a high debit interest rate.
Ein niedriger Sollzins macht es für Unternehmen attraktiv, Kredite für neue Investitionen aufzunehmen.
A low borrowing rate makes it attractive for companies to take out loans for new investments.
